kill_fact: No kill. Every load-bearing number in the bear/value case verifies against primary filings, and the one material error found (share count) runs in the WRONG direction for a kill — it makes the per-share sum-of-the-parts CHEAPER, not dearer. The closest thing to a kill is catalyst decay, and it is real: since the debate, BOTH dated 2026 forcing windows have fired empty. The May 20, 2026 Investor Day (announced 2026-04-21, IR wire) was a standalone-strategy presentation — no sale, spin, or strategic review announced — and the May 21, 2026 Annual Meeting was fully routine: the board's own Class II nominees (Sara Baack, Ligia Torres Fentanes) elected, no Voss Capital nominees, no shareholder proposals, no strategic-alternatives item. Voss (~4.2%, open letter 2026-03-04) remains a non-binding letter-writer with no board seats and no announced board response through 2026-07-01; the next hard governance window is the 2027 meeting. But the bear thesis ALREADY prices this (catalyst_status SOFT_EXTENDED, watch-and-wait), so it corrects the setup rather than refuting it.
corrections: (1) SHARE COUNT (load-bearing, ~25-35% stale): the debate divides every SoP by '~52M shares' — that is the FY2023-era diluted count. Current reality: FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-26) basic weighted-average 39.3M; market cap $2.864B at $75.22 (2026-07-01) implies ~38.1M outstanding; proxy cover ~38.0M as of late March 2026. The Q1 2026 10-Q diluted 46.99M only reaches 47M by adding ~8.0M if-converted shares from the $1B 0.625% converts due 2030 struck at ~$127.04 (priced 2025-08-14 at a 30% premium to $97.72, with capped calls on top) — far out of the money at ~$75. Using 52M shares AND keeping the converts inside net debt double-counts them. Consistently treated (~39M shares, converts as debt), the ADVERSE SoP is ~$125-127/share (not ~$95) and the base ~$135-140 (not ~$105). The value floor is UNDERSTATED in the debate; the correction favors the bulls. (2) PRICE ANCHOR STALE: the stock is $75.22 (2026-07-01 close), not 'near $67' — up ~12% since the debate (52wk range $62.50-$107.91) after the Q1 beat (2026-04-29) and Investor Day, compressing stated upside and weakening the bear's 'Investor Day came and went without re-rating' line. (3) NET DEBT $570M VERIFIED BUT FRAGILE AS 'EXCESS': the Q1 2026 release splits total cash $2,134.4M into unrestricted $1,229.5M / ATM cash $871.2M / restricted $33.7M, against total indebtedness $2,556.2M. ATM cash is operating float for the EFT network, largely funded by short-term/revolver draws — the pairing roughly washes, so ~$420-570M corporate net debt stands, but do NOT treat the headline $2.13B as available cash. (4) REFINANCING HEADWIND THE BEAR MISSED: the EUR 600M 1.375% senior notes (~$693M, sitting in the $971.1M short-term debt at 3/31/26) matured May 2026; rolling that paper from 1.375% to current SOFR/EURIBOR-level rates adds a real interest drag (order of $20M+/yr pre-tax) against the 10-15% adjusted-EPS guide. Liquidity itself is not at issue. (5) REMITTANCE EXCISE TAX NARROWER THAN FRAMED: IRC 4475 (One Big Beautiful Bill, effective transfers after 2025-12-31; IRS proposed regs, Federal Register 2026-04-13; Notice 2025-55 penalty relief) applies at 1% ONLY to cash / money-order / cashier's-check-funded transfers — bank-account and US card-funded transfers are exempt. It taxes exactly Ria's retail-cash core, but it also accelerates migration to Ria Digital (+35% transactions, +42% revenue in Q1 2026), which Euronet owns. Structural pressure verified, not a uniform levy on the whole Money Transfer book. (6) BEAR NUMBERS THAT VERIFY EXACTLY: net income flat $306.3M (FY2024) to $309.5M (FY2025); FY2025 FCF $410.8M vs $615.6M (-33% YoY); FY2025 buybacks $667.7M (~216% of net income — the 'buyback-manufactured EPS' claim is if anything understated) plus another $100M in Q1 2026; FY2025 segment revenues EFT ~$1.28B / Money Transfer ~$1.78B / epay ~$1.19B sum to the reported $4.24B total; Q1 2026 Money Transfer revenue -4% constant currency with transactions down 2% (structural erosion is now in the prints, not just guided); Q1 2026 GAAP diluted EPS $0.83 (-2% YoY) vs adjusted $1.58 (+40%) — the GAAP/adjusted gap the bear attacks is real and widening. WU cohort de-rate verified and WORSE than stated: $7.85 / $2.45B cap (2026-07-01), ~5x forward earnings.
